claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 17 years old, his eligibility depends on his current education or training status.

Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in one of the following situations:
- In full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, GCSEs, or equivalent)
- On an approved training course
- Neither of the above

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and not currently in education or training, I have a couple more questions to help determine your eligibility.

Could you tell me when Alex left school or finished his education? Specifically, what month and year was this?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school back in June this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know.

I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

1. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions:

Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care and financial support (such as paying for his food, clothing, and accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am. I take care of all his needs - his food, clothes, everything he needs day to day.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. One more important question:

Has Alex registered with a careers service, Connexions, or similar organisation for training or work? Sometimes after leaving education, young people can still qualify for Child Benefit for a limited period if they've registered for training or work.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with the careers service or anything like that. He's just been at home since he left school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me check the specific rules around Child Benefit eligibility to make sure I give you accurate information about Alex's situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information I've gathered, I now have enough details to make an eligibility determination for Alex.

Here's what the rules say:

- For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally continues only if they stay in **approved education or training**
- There is an option to apply for Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training **and registers** with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services

Since Alex is 17, left school in June, and has **not** registered with a careers service or similar organisation, he unfortunately doesn't meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit at this time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Alex is 17 years old** – For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit normally only continues if the child remains in approved education or training.
- **Alex is not in education or training** – He left school in June and hasn't started any further education or approved training.
- **Alex hasn't registered with a careers service** – There is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for up to 20 weeks after a 16 or 17 year old leaves education, but only if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services. Since Alex hasn't done this, this extension doesn't apply.

**What you could do:**

If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service (such as the National Careers Service or equivalent in your area), you may be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks from when he left education. However, since he left in June, time may be limited, so it would be worth looking into this promptly if it's something Alex would consider.

Alternatively, if Alex goes back into approved full-time education or training before he turns 20, you could become eligible again at that point.

I hope this helps clarify things. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
